description: Panel uses fixed width:460 capped by maxWidth:100vw, so it fills the screen below 460px (acceptable), but the fixed 460 combined with internal fixed-width label column (130px) leaves only ~120px for values at 250px viewport. Width itself is bounded by maxWidth:100vw so no page scroll, but flag the rigid label column it pairs with (see detail rows).
currentCode: style={{ position:"fixed", top:0, right:0, bottom:0, zIndex:201, width:460, maxWidth:"100vw", background:"#F9FAFB", boxShadow:"-8px 0 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)", display:"flex", flexDirection:"column", fontFamily:"'Inter','Segoe UI',sans-serif" }}
suggestedFix: Keep maxWidth:"100vw" (good) but reduce the paired fixed label column at narrow widths; add a media query: @media (max-width:520px){ /* see detail-row label fix */ }. No change to width:460 needed for desktop.

section: DetailPanel - request details row label column
description: Each detail row uses a fixed 130px min-width label column with no media-query reduction. At a 250px viewport (panel = 100vw = ~250px minus 32px padding ≈ 218px), the 130px label leaves only ~88px for values; combined with the flex row this risks overflow and squeezes the value column. Label width should shrink or rows should stack on narrow screens.
currentCode: {label} {val || "—"}
suggestedFix: Add a class to the row span and reduce via media query, e.g. give the label span className="dp-label" and add: @media (max-width:520px){ .dp-label{ width:auto !important; min-width:90px !important; } } OR stack the row to flexDirection:column at narrow widths. Desktop keeps 130px.

description: Stat grid is repeat(4,1fr). The media query at 900px drops it to 2 columns, but there is NO further stack to a single column below ~560px. At 250px two columns of stat cards (each with 48px icon + 20-22px padding) overflow the container and cause horizontal scroll.
suggestedFix: Add a media query to collapse to 1 column on small screens: @media (max-width:560px){ div[style*="repeat(4,1fr)"]{ grid-template-columns: 1fr !important; } } (matches the existing 900px selector pattern in the <style> block).

description: StatCard uses padding:"20px 22px" with no responsive reduction; combined with a 48px icon and gap:16, the card content (esp. fontSize:28 value) is wide. At narrow widths the padding should scale down to avoid cramping/overflow within the grid cell.
currentCode: <div style={{ background:"#fff", borderRadius:12, border:"1px solid #E5E7EB", padding:"20px 22px", display:"flex", alignItems:"center", gap:16, boxShadow:"0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)" }}>
suggestedFix: Reduce padding/gap on small screens via a class + media query, e.g. add className="statcard" and: @media (max-width:560px){ .statcard{ padding:14px !important; gap:10px !important; } }

description: The data table is wrapped in overflowX:"auto" and the table is width:100% with 7 columns of nowrap cells (CASE ID, DEVOTEE, MOBILE, SERVICE, STATUS, SUBMITTED, action). This is exactly the forbidden sideways-scroll pattern: at narrow widths the table scrolls horizontally instead of collapsing to a stacked list.
suggestedFix: Remove overflowX:"auto" and implement a mobile-collapse pattern: hide the <table> below ~640px (via media query) and render a stacked card/list per record (primary label = fullName + caseReference, with a chevron/Open button), OR convert each row to display:block cards at narrow widths. e.g. add a class to wrapper and: @media (max-width:640px){ .trikala-table{ display:none; } .trikala-cards{ display:flex; flex-direction:column; } } and add a stacked-list renderer.

description: All table header cells force whiteSpace:"nowrap" with fixed 16px horizontal padding; with 7 columns this guarantees the table is wider than a 250px viewport, forcing the parent overflowX scroll. Header row has no mobile-collapse alternative.
suggestedFix: As part of the table-collapse fix, hide <thead> at narrow widths and render labeled stacked rows instead. The nowrap header is acceptable ONLY on desktop; ensure the whole table is replaced by a stacked list below ~640px.

description: The Devotee cell renders fullName and email as real content inside a table that scrolls sideways. These should wrap in a stacked-list layout, not contribute to a wide scrolling table. (No ellipsis here, but the cell lives in the forbidden scroll container.)
currentCode:
{c.fullName}

{c.email}
suggestedFix: In the mobile-collapse list, render fullName as the primary wrapping label and email below it (wordBreak:break-all), inside a block card rather than a table cell. No desktop change.

section: Top nav header - fixed height & horizontal padding with many children
description: Header is a single non-wrapping flex row (height:60, no flexWrap) holding logo, search (maxWidth:440), search button, spacer, Refresh button, admin user, and Logout button. The 560px media query only trims padding/gap; it never wraps or hides items, so at 250px these fixed-size children overflow horizontally.
currentCode: <header style={{ background:"#fff", borderBottom:"1px solid #E5E7EB", height:60, display:"flex", alignItems:"center", padding:"0 28px", gap:16 }}>
suggestedFix: Allow wrapping and auto height on small screens. Add to the <style> block: @media (max-width:560px){ header{ flex-wrap:wrap !important; height:auto !important; padding:10px 14px !important; row-gap:8px !important; } } and let the search input take full width (flex-basis:100%) when wrapped. Desktop unaffected.

section: Top nav header - search wrapper maxWidth
description: Search wrapper uses flex:1 with maxWidth:440 but no min-width:0 guard; inside a non-wrapping header flex row the input plus all other fixed-width buttons exceed 250px. While input itself has box-sizing:border-box and width:100% (good), the surrounding row does not allow it to shrink the header below overflow.
suggestedFix: Add minWidth:0 to allow shrinking: <div style={{ flex:1, minWidth:0, maxWidth:440, position:"relative" }}> and pair with the header flex-wrap media query so the search can take full width on small screens.

section: Top nav header - spacer + duplicate flex:1 pushing buttons
description: An extra flex:1 spacer div sits between the search button and the right-side buttons. In a non-wrapping header this just consumes space on desktop, but at narrow widths it has no effect to prevent overflow; once header wrapping is added this spacer should collapse to avoid an empty wrapped line.
suggestedFix: Hide the spacer on small screens within the header media query, e.g. give it className="nav-spacer" and: @media (max-width:560px){ .nav-spacer{ display:none !important; } }

description: <main> uses padding:"32px 32px 48px". There IS a 900px media query reducing it to 20px 16px 40px, so this is already handled for narrow widths; flagged only to confirm no additional reduction needed below 560px (current value is acceptable).
suggestedFix: No change required — already covered by @media (max-width:900px){ main{ padding:20px 16px 40px !important } }. (Listed for completeness; not a defect.)

section: Table card header - records count row
description: The table-card title row uses padding:"16px 22px" justify space-between with no flex-wrap; the title and '{n} records' are short, so this is low risk, but the 22px horizontal padding does not reduce on small screens and adds to inner width.
currentCode: <div style={{ display:"flex", alignItems:"center", justifyContent:"space-between", padding:"16px 22px", borderBottom:"1px solid #F3F4F6" }}>
suggestedFix: Reduce padding on small screens via a class + media query: add className="tablecard-head" and @media (max-width:560px){ .tablecard-head{ padding:12px 14px !important; } }

section: DetailPanel header padding & status badge row
description: The avatar + name/email + status badge row is a non-wrapping flex (avatar 46px flexShrink:0, status badge flexShrink:0). With the name/email column using minWidth:0 it can shrink, but at 250px the 46px avatar + badge + gaps leave little room; acceptable since middle column shrinks, but padding:"20px 22px 18px" does not reduce on small screens.
suggestedFix: Reduce header padding on narrow screens via class + media query: add className="dp-header" and @media (max-width:520px){ .dp-header{ padding:16px 14px !important; } }
